'''Graham Higman''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Conder |first=Marston D. E. |date=2022 |title=Graham Higman. 19 January 1917—8 April 2008 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2022.0002 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=277–290 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2022.0002 |s2cid=250093355 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (19 January 1917 &ndash; 8 April 2008) was a prominent English [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to [[group theory]].

==Biography==
Higman was born in [[Louth, Lincolnshire]], and attended [[Sutton_High_ School,_Plymouth|Sutton High School, Plymouth]], winning a scholarship to [[Balliol College, Oxford]].<ref name=independent>{{cite web| last = Collins| first = Michael| title = Professor Graham Higman: Leading group theorist| work = Obituaries| publisher = The Independent| date = 2008-05-08| url = https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/professor-graham-higman-leading-group-theorist-822756.html| access-date =2008-10-14 }}</ref> In 1939 he co-founded [[Oxford University Invariant Society|The Invariant Society]], the student mathematics society,<ref>The Early History of the Invariant Society by Robin Wilson, printed in The Invariant (2010), Ben Hoskin</ref> and earned his DPhil from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1941.  His thesis, ''The units of group-rings'', was written under the direction of [[J. H. C. Whitehead]].   
From 1960 to 1984 he was the [[Waynflete Professorships#Waynflete Professors of Pure Mathematics|Waynflete Professor of Pure Mathematics]] at [[Magdalen College, Oxford]].

Higman was awarded the [[Berwick Prizes|Senior Berwick Prize]] in 1962 and the [[De Morgan Medal]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 1974. He was the founder of the [[Journal of Algebra]] and its editor from 1964 to 1984. Higman had 51 D.Phil. students, including [[Jonathan Lazare Alperin]], [[Rosemary A. Bailey]], [[Marston Conder]], [[John Mackintosh Howie]], and [[Peter M. Neumann]].

He was also a [[Methodist local preacher|local preacher]] in the Oxford Circuit of the [[Methodism|Methodist Church]].  During the [[Second World War]] he was a [[conscientious objector]], working at the [[Meteorological Office]] in [[Northern Ireland]] and [[Gibraltar]].

He died in Oxford.<ref name=independent/>
